skills.name: IDEAVO Development - OpenCode

- Create an application or service, add a feature, fix a bug, or refactor code.
- Modify a web interface or add authentication, databases, payments, queues, or storage.
- Prepare, validate, or promote deployments.
- Review performance, accessibility, SEO, security, or quality.
- Investigate CI, GitHub Actions, Vercel, database, or runtime failures.
inputs: User request, repository state, local instructions, stack, validation commands, available MCPs, and operational constraints.
outputs: Implemented change with validation evidence, documented remaining risks, and a clearly stated delivery status.

skills.name: Web Project Bootstrap

skills.name: Containerize a Web Application
skills.summary: Create a reproducible, secure, and operable image for a web application.
skills.whenToUse: - The application has known build and run processes.
inputs: Runtime, commands, ports, dependencies, secrets, and deployment targets.
outputs: Validated Dockerfile, exclusions, documentation, and runtime tests.

skills.name: Dokploy Compose Deployment
skills.summary: Create, promote, and diagnose Dokploy Docker Compose resources with explicit technical names, protected variables, domains, and a master -> preview -> production flow.
skills.whenToUse:
- The service deploys as Docker Compose in Dokploy (`composeType: docker-compose`), with a compatible Dockerfile and `docker-compose.yml`.
- Work follows `master` (development), `preview` (validation), and `production` (live) branches with a promotion PR.
- Environment-identifiable resources and Traefik domains bound to the web service are required.
inputs: Git repository, docker-compose.yml, and compatible Dockerfile.
Dokploy API/panel access and the correct project/environment.
Domains, protected variables, persistence decision, and explicit Production approval.
master (validation) and production (live) branches, with a promotion PR.
outputs: Identifiable Dokploy Docker Compose resources isolated by environment.
Variables stored with safe dotenv quoting and no secrets committed to Git.
HTTPS domains bound to the correct web service.
Documented smoke tests, healthchecks, logs, and rollback.

skills.name: Dokploy Swarm Stack Deployment
skills.summary: Prepare, promote, and diagnose Dokploy/Swarm stacks with verifiable backup gates, API-only builds, independent maintenance, and site/app bindings.
skills.whenToUse:
- The service deploys as a Dokploy/Swarm Stack (`composeType: stack`), not plain Compose or Nixpacks.
- Development, Preview, and Production environments promote fail-closed.
- Per-environment site/app bindings, verifiable native backups, and Swarm task diagnosis are required.
inputs: Git repository or sanitized ZIP snapshot, compatible Stack Compose, and workflow.
Dokploy API/panel access, isolated stacks, site/app domains, and protected variables.
Optional private registry; push and pull permissions must be verified separately.
Persistence, backup/restore, seed, smoke-test, promotion, and Production approval decisions.
outputs: Isolated Dokploy/Swarm stacks promotable from Development -> Preview -> Production.
Reproducible registry-digest builds or explicitly scoped API-only snapshot builds.
Native volume or remote backups with completion evidence or restore rehearsal.
Separate site/app surfaces per environment, bound to the full Swarm service.
Smoke tests, task/log diagnosis, and documented rollback.

skills.name: CI with OpenShip Actions and Self-Hosted Runners
skills.summary: Run CI validation on own infrastructure with OpenShip Actions, in independent mode or with self-hosted runners for GitHub workflows, with a hardened Dokploy alternative.
skills.whenToUse:
- Typecheck, lint, tests, builds, or migration rehearsals need owned infrastructure.
- A native OpenShip workflow and its promotion gates need documentation or validation.
- An independent Dokploy fallback is being assessed without registering GitHub runners.
inputs: An OpenShip instance with Actions (v0.9.0 or later) verified in its dashboard.
An execution destination with known OS, architecture, and tooling.
The instance's GitHub connection for importing workflows and publishing Checks.
An access policy with per-attempt approvals.
outputs: Validation running on own infrastructure with Checks published to GitHub.
Registered, labeled runners in Ready/Idle state.
Per-workflow limited access and recorded approvals.

skills.name: OpenShip Project and Environment Deployment
skills.summary: Operate OpenShip projects with Production and Preview, persistent services, PostgreSQL migrations, verifiable backups, promotion, and rollback.
skills.whenToUse:
- Deploying an application to OpenShip/Atlas.
- Needing Preview and Production environments within one OpenShip project.
- Migrating PostgreSQL and persistent services from Neon, Vercel, or another provider.
- Operating backups, promotion, rollback, or Cloudflare changes.
inputs: Git repository, master/preview/production branches, and an OpenShip-compatible Dockerfile or service definition.
OpenShip MCP access and target workspace/server.
One OpenShip project with internal environments; do not create duplicate Preview projects unless OpenShip requires it.
Data inventory, source PostgreSQL, RPO/RTO, backups, domains, Cloudflare, and explicit Production approval.
outputs: One OpenShip project with isolated Production and Preview environments.
Web, worker/cron, and persistent PostgreSQL services with environment-specific volumes.
Full backup and verified restore rehearsal.
Promotion of the same validated candidate and documented rollback.
DNS/TLS changed only after the new Production is validated.

categories.title: IDE Instructions
categories.description: Instruction and rule files for IDEs and coding agents such as Ideavo, Claude Code, and Codex.

skills.name: Agent Instructions Authoring
skills.summary: Write a neutral, reusable instructions file shared across IDEs and coding agents.
skills.whenToUse:
- The team uses more than one agent or IDE on the same repository.
- Several instruction files exist with diverging rules.
- A single source of conventions is needed for every agent to reference.
inputs: Agents and IDEs in use, team conventions, and tasks routinely delegated to the agent.
outputs: Neutral instructions file with verifiable rules and per-agent references.

skills.name: IDE Instructions Audit
skills.summary: Review existing instruction files to detect outdated, contradictory, or unsafe rules.
skills.whenToUse:
- The agent breaks conventions that are already documented.
- The repository changed stack, commands, or structure.
- Secrets or excessive permissions are suspected in the instructions.
inputs: Current instruction files, actual repository state, and issues reported by the team.
outputs: Prioritized findings report with applied or proposed corrections.

skills.name: Branch Flow in Ideavo
skills.summary: Branch flow desarrollo, preview and production in Ideavo projects, including disjoint-history branches.
skills.whenToUse: - When creating, promoting, integrating or cleaning branches in an Ideavo project whose working branch is `desarrollo`.
inputs: Repository, current branches and SHAs, live environment configuration, and owner authority.
outputs: Documented promotion flow verified per version, with branch status and gate evidence.

skills.name: Ideavo Instructions Setup
skills.summary: Create the Ideavo instructions file with project context, conventions, and boundaries.
skills.whenToUse:
- The repository will be used with Ideavo and has no instructions of its own.
- Existing instructions are outdated compared to the actual project.
- The team repeats the same corrections to the agent in every session.
inputs: Repository structure, build and test commands, code conventions, and operational constraints.
outputs: Versioned and verified Ideavo instructions file committed to the repository.
